Russia travel guide for Arab families

How to plan a first trip to Russia: the two capitals, sample itineraries, the best season, costs, visa rules and practical tips, with links to our detailed English guides.

Why Russia works so well for families from the Gulf

Direct flights from Riyadh, Jeddah, Dubai, Doha and Kuwait reach Moscow in about five hours. Citizens of the six Gulf states enter Russia visa-free, hotels and restaurants are good value, and Moscow and St. Petersburg are safe, clean cities with excellent metros. Halal food is easy to find thanks to large Tatar, Caucasian and Central Asian communities. Start with 10 essential things to know before travelling to Russia and the best things to do in Russia 2026.

The two capitals

  • Moscow: Red Square and the Kremlin, St. Basil's Cathedral, the palatial metro, Gorky Park, Moscow City skyscrapers and family parks such as Dream Island. See the Moscow travel guide 2026 and the 10 best places to visit in Moscow.
  • St. Petersburg: the Hermitage, Peterhof fountains, Catherine Palace, canal cruises and the White Nights in June. See tourism in Saint Petersburg, a comprehensive guide.
  • Beyond the capitals: Kazan, the Muslim-heritage capital of Tatarstan, is a four-hour high-speed train from Moscow; Sochi on the Black Sea adds beaches and mountains.

Sample itineraries

  • 7 days: Moscow only, at a relaxed family pace. See our 7-day Moscow program.
  • 10 days: Moscow (5) → Sapsan high-speed train (4 hours) → St. Petersburg (5). See the 10-day all-inclusive program.
  • 12 days: adds Kazan between the two capitals, ideal for travellers interested in Islamic heritage. See the complete 12-day Russia programme.

Best time to visit

Late May to early September is the family season: long days, 20–28°C and all fountains, parks and river cruises open. June brings the White Nights to St. Petersburg. September is quieter and cheaper with golden autumn colours. Winter (December to February) is cold, around -5 to -15°C in Moscow, but offers snow activities, Christmas lights and the lowest prices; it suits families who want a true winter experience. Avoid the first ten days of January and early May when Russians travel en masse.

What a family trip costs

For a family of four on a 7-day private program with 4-star hotels, a car with driver and an Arabic-speaking guide, expect roughly 3,000–4,500 USD in summer and 2,400–3,600 USD in other seasons, excluding international flights. Sapsan train tickets cost about 40–80 USD per person. International bank cards do not currently work in Russia, so bring cash or let Arcadia handle payments. Full breakdown in a practical guide to the cost of tourism in Russia.

Visa and practical notes

  • Citizens of the six Gulf states enter visa-free. Details in entering Russia for Gulf countries: what you need to know and the Russia visa guide.
  • Register your stay through the hotel within seven working days; hotels do this automatically.
  • Travelling as a group of friends or families? See group trips to Russia, and ask about early-booking discounts.
  • Children under 7 enter most museums free; carry passports for everyone, as they are checked at ticket desks.
  • Download Yandex Maps and Yandex Go (taxi) before arrival; Google Maps works but is less accurate for transport.

Frequently asked questions

Is Russia safe for families now?
Moscow and St. Petersburg remain safe for tourists, with strong police presence and low street crime. We monitor conditions and adjust itineraries if needed.

Do guides speak Arabic?
Yes. Arcadia provides Arabic-speaking guides in both capitals and in Kazan, plus English-speaking guides on request.

How do we pay without Visa or Mastercard?
Bring US dollars or euros to exchange, or prepay the whole program with Arcadia so that hotels, transport, tickets and most meals are covered in advance.

Which is better for children, Moscow or St. Petersburg?
Both. Moscow has more theme parks and modern attractions; St. Petersburg has palaces, fountains and boat trips. A 10-day trip covers both comfortably.
